signals.claim_paraphrase: AI agents can report completion before anyone verifies the actual outcome.
signals.counterposition: Fast exploratory loops can reasonably use provisional completion labels.

signals.claim_paraphrase: Verification is becoming part of the product rather than a final QA step.
signals.counterposition: Not every low-risk workflow warrants heavy evidence collection.
signals.evidence_excerpt: verification became part of the product

signals.claim_paraphrase: Teams can mistake tool access for adoption even when operating behavior has not changed.
signals.counterposition: Access remains a necessary and measurable first step in a staged rollout.
signals.evidence_excerpt: tool access did not change operating behavior

signals.claim_paraphrase: Non-traditional builders need tight feedback loops when AI expands what they can attempt.
signals.counterposition: Feedback loops do not replace engineering fundamentals for reliable systems.
signals.evidence_excerpt: feedback loops matter for reliable systems

signals.claim_paraphrase: A popular post should not be confused with a durable market signal.
signals.counterposition: A one-off post can still expose a useful question worth testing elsewhere.
signals.evidence_excerpt: timing should be measured rather than assumed

signals.claim_paraphrase: The timing gap between X conversations and LinkedIn response is measurable rather than assumed.
signals.counterposition: Different audiences and formats may make cross-platform timing comparisons invalid.

signals.claim_paraphrase: This signal is intentionally outside the configured freshness window.
signals.counterposition: Historical context can still matter when labeled accurately.

candidates.title: Done is not verified
candidates.external_argument: Completion labels are weak evidence unless the workflow preserves a checkable result.
candidates.counterargument: Exploration can move faster with provisional labels when consequences are low and reversible.
candidates.buyer_question: What result did the system actually prove?
candidates.owner_position: Verification belongs in the operating system, not in a celebratory final status.
candidates.proof_needed: One redacted completion report, the failed check, and the correction the owner actually made.
existing_inventory_matches: Prior shortlist: The agent marked it done. What did we verify?
candidates.differentiation: Use a real retained evidence trail rather than another abstract human-in-the-loop claim.
candidates.format_why: A compact evidence sequence can show claim, check, failure, and correction.
hooks: The agent said done. The evidence said otherwise.
Completion is a claim. Verification is the product behavior.
disqualifications: No story without a current redacted artifact

candidates.title: Access is not adoption
candidates.external_argument: Tool availability is not evidence that a team changed how it decides or works.
candidates.counterargument: Access is still a necessary first-stage rollout metric.
candidates.buyer_question: What changed in the operating workflow after access was granted?
candidates.owner_position: Measure the changed decision or workflow, while conceding that access is only the first rung.
candidates.proof_needed: One publicly describable workflow change and outcome measure with no employer or client detail.
existing_inventory_matches: Prior shortlist: Access versus actual adoption
candidates.differentiation: Ground the distinction in an operating decision rather than another maturity framework.
candidates.format_why: A concise operator story can invite comparable workflow examples.
hooks: Your rollout metric may be measuring access, not adoption.
The hard part starts after everyone gets the login.
disqualifications: No broad enterprise claim from one example

candidates.title: The non-traditional builder feedback loop
candidates.external_argument: AI expands who can attempt product work, raising the value of disciplined feedback loops.
candidates.counterargument: Expanded access does not erase engineering fundamentals or reliability obligations.
candidates.buyer_question: Which judgment step cannot be delegated in this build?
candidates.owner_position: AI expands capability; standards, feedback, and judgment determine whether the result becomes useful.
candidates.proof_needed: One small build-test-adjust sequence with a before and after artifact.
candidates.differentiation: Show the quality loop and its tradeoff instead of leading with credentials.
candidates.format_why: The argument needs the owner's actual moment and proof before a format is locked.
hooks: No CS degree does not mean no standards.
AI expanded what I could build. The feedback loop decided whether it was real.
disqualifications: Do not imply universal credential erosion

candidates.title: Test the lag instead of asserting it
candidates.external_argument: X can surface an argument early, but transfer to LinkedIn must be measured rather than assumed.
candidates.counterargument: Audience and format differences may make the platforms incomparable.
candidates.buyer_question: Does an emerging X argument produce qualified LinkedIn conversations?
candidates.owner_position: Treat timing as an experiment with matched outcomes, not as algorithm folklore.
candidates.proof_needed: A preregistered matched publishing test and qualified-response measures.
candidates.differentiation: Publish the test design and uncertainty rather than a viral-timing claim.
candidates.format_why: A compact experiment statement can invite other operators' measurement approaches.
hooks: The lag might be an edge. That is not the same as proving it.
A popular X post is not a LinkedIn brief.
